A2.text:
Orkhan is a student. He lives in a flat with his friends Elvin and Tural. On Sunday, his mother is coming to visit for the first time.

“Let's cook dinner for her,” Orkhan said. “Dushbara soup, from scratch!”

They found a recipe online. They bought all the ingredients: meat, onions, flour and herbs. Elvin made the small dumplings. Tural began to chop the onions and cried a lot. Orkhan put the soup on the cooker to simmer.

But there was a problem. Every boy wanted to help. Elvin added salt. Ten minutes later, Tural added more seasoning. Then Orkhan added salt too. Nobody watched the pot, and the bottom of the soup was burnt.

At six o'clock, Orkhan's mother arrived. She tasted the soup and her eyes opened wide.

“Too many cooks spoil the broth,” she laughed. “Who made this?”

“All of us,” said Orkhan sadly.

His mother looked in the fridge. There were some leftovers: rice, eggs and tomatoes. In twenty minutes, she made a delicious dinner. The boys ate everything.

“I know you have a lot on your plate with exams,” she said. “Next time, just call me.”

After dinner, the three boys did all the washing-up. Orkhan's mother sat and drank tea.

options: Three friends try to cook for a mother, and she saves dinner
A mother teaches a cooking class
Three friends buy food in a café
questions.why: Their soup goes wrong, and his mother makes dinner from leftovers.

options: She wants to cook for them because they are busy students

B1.text:
Orkhan shared a small flat in Yasamal with two friends from university, Elvin and Tural. When his mother announced she was coming from Shamakhi for Sunday dinner, the three of them decided to impress her. “No takeaway,” Orkhan said. “We'll make dushbara from scratch, like my grandmother does.”

They found a recipe on a cooking channel and wrote a long shopping list. On Saturday they bought every ingredient: lamb, onions, flour, dried mint, saffron. Elvin, who had the most patient fingers, folded more than a hundred tiny dumplings. Tural agreed to chop the onions and spent twenty minutes crying over the cutting board. Orkhan was in charge of the broth, which had to simmer gently for two hours.

The trouble was that nobody trusted anybody else. Elvin tasted the broth and added salt. Tural tasted it later and added more seasoning, plus a spoonful of pepper “for character”. Orkhan, without asking, added salt for the third time. Then they all went to watch football, and nobody noticed the smell until the bottom of the pot was burnt black.

His mother arrived at six. She lifted the lid, tasted a spoonful and coughed politely.

“Well,” she said, “too many cooks spoil the broth. How many of you salted it?”

Three hands went up.

She laughed so hard she had to sit down. Then she rolled up her sleeves and opened the fridge. Within half an hour, she had turned some leftovers — yesterday's rice, four eggs, a few tomatoes and Elvin's beautiful dumplings — into a meal the boys still talk about.

“You three have a lot on your plate with exams,” she said, kissing her son's head. “Cooking can wait.”

“At least let us do the washing-up,” said Orkhan.

“Oh, that was never a question,” his mother replied.

options: Too many helpers ruin the soup, but the mother saves the evening
questions.why: The soup is too salty and burnt; she makes dinner from leftovers.

questions.why: “Then they all went to watch football.”

questions.why: “...a few tomatoes and Elvin's beautiful dumplings.”

options: From the beginning, using basic ingredients
questions.why: They made everything themselves, “like my grandmother does”.

B2.text:
When Orkhan's mother rang to say she was coming in from Shamakhi for Sunday dinner, the three students sharing his cramped flat in Yasamal held what Tural solemnly called an emergency summit. Takeaway was ruled out at once as an admission of defeat. “We're making dushbara,” Orkhan declared, “completely from scratch. Exactly the way my grandmother does it.”

The recipe came from a cooking channel run by a cheerful woman in Sheki who made everything look effortless. Saturday was spent hunting down each ingredient — fatty lamb, onions, flour, dried mint, a pinch of saffron that cost more than Tural's lunch. Elvin, who possessed the patience of a watchmaker, folded over a hundred dumplings the size of hazelnuts. Tural volunteered to chop the onions and spent twenty minutes weeping theatrically over the cutting board. Orkhan took charge of the broth, which, according to the woman from Sheki, needed to simmer for two hours over the lowest possible flame.

The fatal flaw in the operation was trust. Elvin tasted the broth and quietly added salt. An hour later, Tural tasted it, decided it lacked “personality” and threw in a generous amount of seasoning. Orkhan, unaware of either intervention, salted it for a third time. Then all three drifted off to watch a football match, and by the time anyone noticed the smell, the bottom of the pot was burnt beyond rescue.

His mother arrived punctually at six. She lifted the lid, sampled a spoonful and maintained an expression of heroic neutrality.

“Too many cooks spoil the broth,” she observed at last. “Out of interest, how many of you added salt?”

Three hands rose slowly.

She laughed until she had to wipe her eyes. Then, without a word of complaint, she pushed up her sleeves and inspected the fridge. Half an hour later the leftovers — yesterday's rice, four eggs, some tired tomatoes and Elvin's immaculate dumplings — had been transformed into the best meal the flat had ever seen.

“You have a lot on your plate this term,” she said, ruffling her son's hair. “The cooking can wait until summer.”

“At least let us handle the washing-up,” Orkhan offered.

His mother poured herself a glass of tea and settled into the only comfortable chair. “My darling,” she said, “I was counting on it.”

questions.q: What is the source of the boys' failure?
options: Each boy secretly salting the soup without telling the others
questions.why: “The fatal flaw in the operation was trust.”
